title: Record Short Superpermutations on 8, 9, and 10 Symbols Beating Egan’s 2018 Bound
whyItMatters: Beats Greg Egan’s 8-year-old 2018 upper bound on minimum superpermutation lengths for n = 8, 9, and 10 symbols, solving an Epoch AI FrontierMath: Open Problems combinatorics challenge.
summary: A superpermutation on n symbols is a string containing every one of the n! permutations as a contiguous substring; for n ≥ 6 the minimum length is open, and Greg Egan’s 2018 construction held the standing upper bound for n ≥ 8. On July 26, 2026, following Uku Raudvere’s improved n = 8 construction, William Echols used OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol at xhigh reasoning in an interactive Codex session to construct explicit superpermutations beating Egan’s upper bound for n = 9 (length ≤ 408,965) and n = 10 (length ≤ 4,037,046). Epoch AI’s exact verifier confirmed all n! contiguous permutation windows, marking the FrontierMath: Open Problems challenge solved.
technicalHighlights: Constructs explicit verified superpermutations strictly beating Greg Egan’s 2018 upper bound for n = 8 (≤ 46,204), n = 9 (≤ 408,965), and n = 10 (≤ 4,037,046).
William Echols generated the n = 9 and n = 10 record sequences in an interactive Codex session powered by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh reasoning) on July 26, 2026.
Exact programmatic verification confirms zero missing permutations across all 10! = 3,628,800 contiguous windows.
caveats: The n = 8 breakthrough was first posted by Uku Raudvere before William Echols and GPT-5.6 Sol rapidly extended it to n = 9 and n = 10 the same day; Epoch AI noted GPT-5.6 Sol retrieved those newly posted sequences during its July 27 pre-release test, counting the challenge solved because AI co-created the n = 9, 10 constructions after benchmark acceptance.

scoreRationale.foundational: Improves an 8-year-old combinatorial upper bound on superpermutation lengths across n = 8, 9, 10 with potential generalization to all n ≥ 8.
scoreRationale.ripple: Highlights rapid human–AI combinatorial construction in interactive coding-agent loops on open FrontierMath problems.
scoreRationale.verification: Unconditionally verified by exact finite substring enumeration checking all n! permutations.
scoreRationale.velocity: Extended from n = 8 to n = 9 and n = 10 within a single day using GPT-5.6 Sol in Codex.
